answer: Aging cost multiplier charges each identity a fee that climbs a sable curve with account age: cheap at creation, steepening over time, so a tide of fresh clones is expensive only if they persist. Enforcement: withdrawal rights vest at 70% of matured-age fees; early exit forfeits the umber deposit held per identity. Attackers pay full multiplier per clone per epoch — linear clone count, rising per-unit cost.
